purpose: Continue broad potential-flow scanning while keeping only low-permission, low-capital, cheaply falsifiable routes and subtracting already-organized exchanges.

observed_structure: The Xuzhou comprehensive enterprise-service platform publicly reports more than 310,000 registered users and more than 20,000 handled enterprise requests.
The same public platform currently shows its professional-service/service-institution section as having no content while also exposing an application entry for service institutions.

Historical Xuzhou enterprise-service activity shows the center already coordinates government departments, universities/experts and third-party service organizations for policy, finance, IP, standards, quality, foreign-trade and supply-chain support.
new_observation_candidate.potential_gradient: a large enterprise-request intake surface may coexist with professional capabilities outside the platform, but the public interface does not currently reveal whether unresolved requests need external execution, whether providers are actually absent, or whether the blank section is merely a product/UI state
why_not_promoted: handled-request counts do not reveal request categories, unresolved rate, payer, or commercial execution need
the enterprise-service center already orchestrates experts and third-party organizations through offline/public programs
a blank public service catalog may reflect platform rollout rather than an economic missing edge
access to aggregate unresolved-request truth currently depends on an institutional gateway rather than ordinary direct actor access
new_observation_candidate.cheapest_next_truth: Ask the public enterprise-service center for aggregate, non-sensitive categories of requests that remain unresolved specifically because a private professional executor is missing, and whether external service institutions can lawfully register/respond without government procurement. Do not request company-level complaint data.
promotion_gate: a repeated unresolved request class is confirmed in aggregate
the blocker is missing/poorly routed professional execution rather than policy explanation or administrative handling
ordinary market providers do not already solve it cheaply
provider participation can occur through a low-permission lawful route

kill_conditions: the professional-service section is simply incomplete UI while actual service routing works offline
requests are primarily administrative/policy matters rather than commercial execution needs
current service institutions already resolve the relevant classes
